content: One to two sentence professional summary. Keep it factual — degree, main domain, strongest 2-3 signal areas. This renders at the top of every resume.

Sysadmin-voice summary. Lead with your sysadmin credential/degree, then your strongest admin signal (Windows/Linux, AD, M365, helpdesk scale, etc.). Used only when job is classified as sysadmin track.

SOC/security-voice summary. Lead with security credential, then strongest security signal (SIEM, threat detection, incident response, frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK). Used only when job is classified as soc track.
Universal fallback summary covering all tracks briefly. Used when no track-specific summary is a better fit.

**Job Title — Company Name** | City, Country | Jan 2023 – Present
- Strong, metric-driven bullet. Action verb + what you did + result or scale.
- Second bullet. Keep each to one line if possible.
- Third bullet only if genuinely distinct from above.
- Additional detail bullet for the same role. Lower priority so it only appears if quota allows. Same group_key as exp_001 so it renders as a continuation bullet, not a separate heading.

**Previous Title — Previous Company** | City, Country | Jun 2021 – Dec 2022
- Bullet focused on transferable skills relevant to your target roles.
- Keep bullets honest and specific. Avoid vague verbs like 'assisted' or 'helped'.
**Project Name** — One sentence on what it is and the tech stack. This is the header bullet, high priority, always shows if the project is selected.
- Detail bullet for the same project: specific technical implementation, scale, or outcome. Lower priority — shows only if quota allows. Same group_key as proj_001.
**Second Project** — What it does, why it matters, stack. Keep the description job-relevant — lead with the signal the project demonstrates (automation, security, devops, etc.).
